9_1_ga_shakespeare_vr.description: Genetic algorithm evolving random strings toward a target phrase — selection, crossover, and mutation producing Shakespeare. Based on Nature of Code Ch.9.
9_1_ga_shakespeare_vr.name: GA Shakespeare (Basic)
9_1_ga_shakespeare_vr.qfep_connection: A population of random strings breeding toward a line of Shakespeare — selection, crossover, mutation, and gibberish converging on poetry. The monkeys-at-typewriters joke made rigorous: with fitness and inheritance, the monkeys win in minutes.

9_2_smart_rockets_basic_vr.description: Basic smart rockets evolving thrust vectors to reach a target — simplified version of genetic algorithm-driven rocket navigation. Based on Nature of Code Ch.9.
9_2_smart_rockets_basic_vr.name: Smart Rockets (Basic)
9_2_smart_rockets_basic_vr.qfep_connection: Rockets evolving their thrust schedules toward a target — no rocket learns, the POPULATION does, the crashed generations composting into the trajectories of the next. Guidance grown, not derived.

9_3_smart_rockets_vr.description: Rockets evolving to reach a target through genetic algorithm — selection, crossover, mutation visible in real-time. Based on Nature of Code Ch.9.
9_3_smart_rockets_vr.name: Smart Rockets (Genetic Algorithm)
9_3_smart_rockets_vr.qfep_connection: Genetic algorithms as population-level F-minimization — fitness IS negative free energy. Mutation injects λ (entropy); selection reduces F (keeps what works). The population explores the edge of chaos between exploitation and exploration.

9_4_interactive_selection_vr.description: User-driven evolutionary selection — choose which organisms survive and reproduce, experiencing artificial selection firsthand. Based on Nature of Code Ch.9.
9_4_interactive_selection_vr.name: Interactive Selection
9_4_interactive_selection_vr.qfep_connection: Evolution with you as the fitness function — organisms breed, and the ones YOU point at survive. Aesthetic selection: the algorithm supplies variation, you supply desire, and the population drifts toward your taste. Darwin's engine with a human at the tiller.

9_5_evolving_bloops_vr.description: Organisms evolving size, speed, and behavior through natural selection pressure. Survival of the fittest visualized. Based on Nature of Code Ch.9.
9_5_evolving_bloops_vr.name: Evolving Bloops

9_6_ga_shakespeare_annotated_vr.description: Annotated version of the genetic algorithm Shakespeare demo — with explanatory labels showing fitness, mutation rate, and generation progress. Based on Nature of Code Ch.9.
9_6_ga_shakespeare_annotated_vr.name: GA Shakespeare (Annotated)
9_6_ga_shakespeare_annotated_vr.qfep_connection: The Shakespeare GA slowed down and annotated — every selection, crossover, and mutation narrated as it happens. The same miracle as 9_1, but with the hood open: evolution as a legible procedure rather than a magic trick.

anomaly_detection.description: Outlier detection algorithms — isolation forests, statistical boundaries, autoencoder reconstruction error. Finding what doesn't belong.
anomaly_detection.name: Anomaly Detection
anomaly_detection.qfep_connection: Anomalies are high-F surprises — data points that the F-model cannot predict. Detection algorithms learn the boundary between expected E(S) and genuine novelty. The queer reading: who counts as anomalous depends on whose F-model defines normal.

attention_mechanisms.description: Transformer attention visualization — query-key-value matrices, attention weights as connection strengths. See what the model attends to.
attention_mechanisms.name: Attention Mechanisms
attention_mechanisms.qfep_connection: Attention IS selective F-allocation — the model learns which inputs to weight heavily (low F surprise) and which to ignore (high E(S) noise). Self-attention computes relevance dynamically, adapting the F-model to each input.

axiom_garden.description: An L-System garden game — grow plants from axiom strings, navigate a turtle through branching structures, overcome obstacles with evolved grammar rules. Formal languages become living landscapes.
axiom_garden.name: Axiom Garden
axiom_garden.qfep_connection: An L-system garden played as a game — write axiom strings, steer a turtle, and grow plants from grammar. The lsystems chapter wearing gloves: sentence-becomes-forest as something you cultivate rather than watch.

clustering_algorithms.description: K-Means, Agglomerative, and DBSCAN clustering side by side — watch three different strategies for finding groups in data. Same points, different assumptions, different results.
clustering_algorithms.name: Clustering Algorithms
clustering_algorithms.qfep_connection: Three ways to find groups nobody labelled — K-means voting with centroids, agglomerative merging neighbors, DBSCAN following density. Side by side they confess the secret of unsupervised learning: 'cluster' is not a fact, it is an ALGORITHM'S OPINION about nearness, and the opinions differ.

computer_vision.description: Computer vision pipeline visualization — from raw pixels through feature extraction to classification. See how machines learn to see: edges, textures, objects.
computer_vision.name: Computer Vision
computer_vision.qfep_connection: The vision pipeline laid end to end — raw pixels to edges to features to labels. Sight as a supply chain: each stage consumes the last one's output, and 'seeing a cat' turns out to be the top floor of a factory of thresholds.

computer_vision_vr.description: Interactive image processing with spatial convolution filters
computer_vision_vr.name: ComputerVision_VR
computer_vision_vr.qfep_connection: Convolution made spatial — a filter sliding across an image, and you inside the sliding. The room where a machine first *sees*: not by understanding, but by sweeping the same small question (is there an edge here? a corner?) across every position until a picture becomes a field of answers.

convolutional_neural_networks.description: CNN architecture visualization — convolutional filters, pooling layers, and feature maps. See how spatial hierarchies emerge from learned kernels scanning across input data.
convolutional_neural_networks.name: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs)
convolutional_neural_networks.qfep_connection: A 3x3 window drags across the input grid and feature maps light up beneath it; pooling then discards most of what was computed, keeping only maxima. This is what a CNN calls seeing: one small prejudice — the kernel — applied everywhere, followed by aggressive forgetting.

convolutional_neural_networks_cnns_vr.description: Walkable CNN architecture with interactive kernels
convolutional_neural_networks_cnns_vr.name: ConvolutionalNeuralNetworksCNNs_VR
convolutional_neural_networks_cnns_vr.qfep_connection: The walkable CNN — kernels you can grab, feature maps stacking from edges to textures to parts to faces. The architecture that taught machines to see by insisting the same detector works everywhere: translation invariance as a built-in belief, the eye's humility written into the weights.

decision_boundary_viewer.description: 2D classification with live decision boundary — two clusters of points separated by a linear classifier (w1*x + w2*y + bias > 0). Background colored by classification region, data points as bright dots, yellow boundary line. VR sliders for w1, w2, bias with live accuracy display.
decision_boundary_viewer.name: Decision Boundary Viewer

dimensionality_reduction.description: High-dimensional data projected to lower dimensions — PCA, t-SNE, and UMAP approaches compared. Finding the essential structure hidden in high-dimensional chaos.
dimensionality_reduction.name: Dimensionality Reduction
dimensionality_reduction.qfep_connection: PCA, t-SNE, and UMAP flattening high-dimensional clouds into maps you can read — each with its own loyalty: PCA to variance, t-SNE to neighborhoods, UMAP to structure. Every flattening lies; each lies differently; choosing the lie is the craft.

enhanced_kmeans.description: Interactive K-means clustering visualization with adjustable k, colored cluster assignments, and centroid movement animation.
enhanced_kmeans.name: Enhanced K-Means Clustering
enhanced_kmeans.qfep_connection: K-means IS iterative F-minimization — centroids move to minimize within-cluster variance. Each step reduces the system's free energy until convergence. K itself is a λ-like parameter: too few clusters = underfitting, too many = overfitting.

ensemble_methods.description: Ensemble learning visualization — multiple weak learners combining into a strong one. Bagging, boosting, and stacking: the wisdom of crowds applied to algorithms.
ensemble_methods.name: Ensemble Methods
ensemble_methods.qfep_connection: Weak learners voting their way to strength — bagging, boosting, forests of shallow opinions outperforming a single deep one. The statistics of the committee: errors that cancel when they're uncorrelated. Democracy as a variance-reduction technique.

evolved_creatures.description: Physics-based creature evolution inspired by Karl Sims — bipedal bodies evolve locomotion through genetic algorithms. Morphology and behavior co-evolve, producing creatures that learn to walk through selection pressure.
evolved_creatures.name: Evolved Creatures (Karl Sims)

evolved_creatures_v2.description: Second-generation evolved creatures — improved physics-based creature evolution with more complex body plans and neural network controllers. Evolution as iterative design.
evolved_creatures_v2.name: Evolved Creatures v2

evolving_creatures_ea.description: Evolutionary algorithms demo — creatures evolving body plans and behaviors through selection, crossover, and mutation. A hands-on look at how evolution works as an optimization process.
evolving_creatures_ea.name: Evolving Creatures (EA)
evolving_creatures_ea.qfep_connection: Creatures evolving bodies and behaviors together — morphology and control co-adapting, gaits discovered rather than designed. Karl Sims' lineage: the search space widened until evolution invents not just answers but the bodies that carry them.

evolving_flowers.description: Flowers evolving color, petal count, and shape through aesthetic selection — beauty as a fitness function. Interactive evolution where the user is the selection pressure.
evolving_flowers.name: Evolving Flowers

evolvingflowers.description: genome = {petals, color_hue, symmetry, L-system_rules, branch_angle}; fitness = symmetry + vibrancy + complexity
evolvingflowers.name: evolvingflowers

explainable_ai.description: Making AI decisions interpretable — feature importance, attention maps, and explanation methods. The critical question: not just what the model predicts, but why.
explainable_ai.name: Explainable AI (XAI)
explainable_ai.qfep_connection: Feature importance, attention maps, saliency — the instruments that ask a trained model WHY. The gallery's accountability bench: partial, honest, contestable answers from systems that owe them.

explainable_ai_xai_vr.description: Interactive SHAP, LIME, and Grad-CAM explanations
explainable_ai_xai_vr.name: ExplainableAIXAI_VR
explainable_ai_xai_vr.qfep_connection: SHAP, LIME, Grad-CAM — the instruments that ask a black box *why*, and get partial, honest, contestable answers. The accountability room: after seven chambers of learning that works without understanding, this one insists the machine show its reasons. Not because the reasons are the truth, but because a decision no one can question is a decision no one can refuse.

feature_engineering.description: Feature engineering visualization — transforming raw data into useful representations. The art of asking the right questions of your data before the model does.
feature_engineering.name: Feature Engineering
feature_engineering.qfep_connection: The unglamorous craft that decides most outcomes — raw data reshaped into representations a model can use. The lesson veterans learn: the model gets the credit, but the features did the work.

fine_tuning.description: Transfer learning and fine-tuning visualization — taking a pre-trained model and adapting it to a new task by updating select layers. The efficient path from general knowledge to specific expertise.
fine_tuning.name: Fine-Tuning
fine_tuning.qfep_connection: A pre-trained model bent to a new task — most weights kept, the last layers re-learned. Transfer learning's central economy: competence is expensive to grow and cheap to adapt, so intelligence becomes an inheritance.

fine_tuning_vr.description: Transfer learning tower with frozen and trainable layers
fine_tuning_vr.name: FineTuning_VR
fine_tuning_vr.qfep_connection: A network as a tower with padlocks: frozen storeys keep their inherited weights while gradients flow only through the unlocked top. Transfer learning staged as property law — most of the model is estate, and 'learning' happens in the floors you are permitted to renovate.

gans.description: GAN visualization — generator and discriminator locked in adversarial training. One creates, the other critiques, and from this competition emerges the ability to generate realistic data.
gans.name: Generative Adversarial Networks
gans.qfep_connection: The generator-discriminator duel at gallery scale — forgery and detection training each other up. Two ignorances pressed together until the counterfeit passes.

generative_adversarial_networks_gans_vr.description: Spatial GAN arena with generator and discriminator zones
generative_adversarial_networks_gans_vr.name: GenerativeAdversarialNetworksGANs_VR
generative_adversarial_networks_gans_vr.qfep_connection: Two networks locked in a duel — a generator forging samples, a discriminator calling the fakes — each making the other better until the forgeries pass. Creation as adversarial pressure, art from an arms race. The world room's unsettling proof that convincing can be reached without ever understanding.

genetic_algorithm.description: Advanced neuroevolution ecosystem with speciation — populations split into species, compete for resources, and evolve distinct strategies. Punctuated equilibrium and adaptive radiation in code.
genetic_algorithm.name: Evolutionary Ecosystem
genetic_algorithm.qfep_connection: Neuroevolution with speciation — populations splitting into protected species so new ideas survive infancy. NEAT's insight: innovation needs shelter, because a fresh mutation loses every fight until it matures. Evolution discovering the nursery.

gradient_descent.description: Gradient descent optimization demo — a ball rolling downhill on a loss surface, following the steepest path to the minimum. The foundational optimization algorithm behind all of deep learning.
gradient_descent.name: Gradient Descent
gradient_descent.qfep_connection: Form-finding's engine, isolated: a ball rolling downhill on a loss surface, always stepping against the slope toward the nearest low point. The same descent that trains a network here shapes a form — the settling mesh, the hanging chain, all of it is this ball, finding a minimum it cannot see the whole of by only ever feeling the ground beneath its feet.

gradient_descent_landscape.description: 3D loss surface with a ball rolling down to the minimum — gradient descent visualization. ImmediateMesh surface colored green at minima, red at peaks. Adjustable learning rate slider and reset button. Trail of breadcrumb spheres shows the optimization path.
gradient_descent_landscape.name: Gradient Descent Landscape

joint_learn_walk.description: RL agent learning to walk — reward shaping, policy gradient, emergent locomotion. Joints discover coordinated movement through trial and error.
joint_learn_walk.name: Joint Learn Walk (Reinforcement Learning)
joint_learn_walk.qfep_connection: Reinforcement learning as embodied F-minimization — the agent builds an internal model through interaction, reducing surprise about its own body. Emergent locomotion is the system discovering its own edge of chaos: coordinated movement from noisy exploration.

kmeans_simple.description: Simplified K-means clustering demonstration — a minimal version showing the core iterative assignment-and-update loop.
kmeans_simple.name: K-Means Simple
kmeans_simple.qfep_connection: K-means at its most minimal — guess centers, assign points, move centers, repeat. The clustering loop stripped to its two-step heartbeat, small enough to hold in the eye.

learn_world_stacked.description: Stacked learning environment — multiple ML models layered together, each learning from the previous layer's output. Meta-learning through hierarchical composition.
learn_world_stacked.name: Learn World (Stacked)
learn_world_stacked.qfep_connection: Multiple models stacked, each learning from the layer below — the chapter's architecture-of-architectures, where one learner's output is another's raw world. Depth as the whole trick: no single layer understands anything, and the stack, somehow, does.

loss_function_comparator.description: Same dataset, three different loss functions applied simultaneously. MSE (smooth bowl), Huber (outlier-robust), and adversarial (deceptive valleys). Gradient descent balls roll on each surface, arriving at different answers. The landscape is not given — it is authored.
loss_function_comparator.name: Loss Function Comparator

lstms.description: Long Short-Term Memory network visualization — gates (forget, input, output) controlling information flow through time. The architecture that solved vanishing gradients and enabled sequence modeling.
lstms.name: LSTMs
lstms.qfep_connection: The LSTM cell with its gates labelled — forget, input, output, a memory that curates itself. Remembering as an act of selective forgetting, drawn as plumbing.

lstms_vr.description: Interactive LSTM cell with walkable memory flow
lstms_vr.name: LSTMs_VR
lstms_vr.qfep_connection: A memory cell you can walk through — gates deciding what to keep, what to forget, what to let out. The LSTM is the chapter's answer to time: a network that carries a thread of context forward, forgetting on purpose so the important thing survives. Memory as a valve, not a vault.

neural_network_visualization.description: Layered neural network with visible activations, weights as line thickness, forward pass animation. See how information transforms through layers.
neural_network_visualization.name: Neural Network Visualization
neural_network_visualization.qfep_connection: Neural networks learn F-models through gradient descent — each weight update reduces prediction error. Overfitting = F too low (memorization); regularization = intentional λ (noise tolerance). Generalization lives at the edge of chaos between memorization and randomness.

neural_networks.description: Feedforward neural network with configurable layer sizes — visible activations, weighted connections, and forward pass animation. Watch information transform through layers of weighted sums and activations.
neural_networks.name: Neural Networks
neural_networks.qfep_connection: A feedforward network with visible activations — signal flowing layer to layer, weights as living wires. The blind adjuster from the ML chapter, here held still enough to watch think.

neural_networks_vr.description: Walkable neural network with visible weights and backpropagation
neural_networks_vr.name: NeuralNetworks_VR
neural_networks_vr.qfep_connection: The network turned inside out and made walkable — weights hanging in the air as visible thicknesses, activations lighting up as you pass, and backpropagation running the error backward through the whole structure like a confession travelling upstream. The primitive of deep learning shown honestly: not a brain, but a landscape of numbers that adjusts itself by measuring how wrong it just was.

nlp.description: NLP pipeline visualization — tokenization, embedding, and sequence modeling. How machines process text: from strings of characters to vectors of meaning.
nlp.name: Natural Language Processing
nlp.qfep_connection: The language pipeline — tokenization, embedding, sequence modeling — words becoming vectors becoming predictions. The uncomfortable center: meaning handled as geometry, nearness in a space no one can visit.

non_teleological_evolution.description: Bodies exist in a space with no fitness function. They reproduce based on proximity and energy (gained by exploring, lost by existing). Forms diversify without goal or optimization — just drift, variation, and persistence. No best creature. No progress narrative.
non_teleological_evolution.name: Non-Teleological Evolution

optimization_algorithms.description: Comparison of optimization algorithms — SGD, Adam, RMSprop, and others navigating loss landscapes. See why some optimizers dance while others plod.
optimization_algorithms.name: Optimization Algorithms
optimization_algorithms.qfep_connection: SGD, Adam, RMSprop racing down the same loss landscape — momentum, adaptive steps, and raw descent taking different paths to different valleys. The chapter's marble multiplied into a field of runners: even blind downhill has schools of technique.

pca_visualization.description: Principal Component Analysis — high-dimensional data projected onto principal axes. Shows variance capture and dimensionality reduction in 3D.
pca_visualization.name: PCA Visualization
pca_visualization.qfep_connection: PCA is pure F-minimization through dimensionality reduction — finding the axes of maximum variance and discarding the rest. Compression of high-dimensional E(S) into the most informative low-dimensional F-model.

perceptron_playground.description: Single neuron with adjustable weights — the simplest possible neural network. Drag sliders to change w1, w2, and bias, watch the decision boundary shift on a 2D scatter plot. Misclassified points get white corners so you can see the perceptron learning.
perceptron_playground.name: Perceptron Playground

random_forest_visualization.description: Visual representation of random forest ensemble — multiple decision trees voting on classification, showing how diversity improves accuracy.
random_forest_visualization.name: Random Forest Visualization

random_walker_machine.description: Random walk simulation — agents taking stochastic steps, demonstrating how randomness underlies exploration in ML. From Brownian motion to Monte Carlo methods.
random_walker_machine.name: Random Walker Machine
random_walker_machine.qfep_connection: Three hundred walkers, each carrying twelve weights, ranked by fitness every two hundred frames while temperature dilutes their conviction with noise. Evolution as a leaderboard with amnesia: only the top twenty are drawn, the rest walk unseen, and the targets themselves drift on noise.

recommendation_systems.description: Collaborative and content-based filtering — how algorithms predict what you'll like based on what similar people liked. The math behind Netflix suggestions.
recommendation_systems.name: Recommendation Systems
recommendation_systems.qfep_connection: Collaborative and content-based filtering — you are what similar people liked, or what your history resembles. The algorithm that curates most of what most people see: prediction of taste, quietly becoming production of taste.

reinforcement_learning.description: RL agent exploring an environment — reward signals, policy updates, and the exploration-exploitation tradeoff. Learning from consequences rather than examples.
reinforcement_learning.name: Reinforcement Learning
reinforcement_learning.qfep_connection: An agent learning from reward alone — explore, get scored, update the policy, repeat. Learning with no teacher but consequence: the landscape isn't labelled, it's LIVED, and the map appears only in the walking.

shape_learner_2d.description: Genetic algorithm + cellular automaton hybrid learning target shapes in 2D. Evolution discovers the CA rules that produce desired patterns — emergence guided by selection.
shape_learner_2d.name: Shape Learner (2D)
shape_learner_2d.qfep_connection: A genetic algorithm breeding cellular-automaton rules until their grown patterns match a target shape — evolution TEACHING emergence. Two chapters shaking hands: the GA supplies desire, the CA supplies growth, and form appears from rules nobody wrote.

shape_learner_3d.description: 3D version of the GA+CA shape learner — evolving cellular automaton rules to produce target 3D structures. Emergence in three dimensions guided by evolutionary pressure.
shape_learner_3d.name: Shape Learner (3D)
shape_learner_3d.qfep_connection: The GA+CA shape learner in three dimensions — evolved automaton rules growing target volumes. Morphogenesis as a search problem: the recipe is found, not designed, and the body builds itself.

spotlight_attention.description: Spotlight model of attention — a focused beam illuminating selected elements while others fade. The cognitive psychology model that inspired transformer attention mechanisms.
spotlight_attention.name: Spotlight Attention
spotlight_attention.qfep_connection: Attention as a spotlight — one beam, serially sweeping, illuminating what cognition currently holds. The older psychology of focus: attention as a scarce resource pointed at one thing at a time.

svm_visualization.description: SVM hyperplane separator with support vectors highlighted. Shows maximum margin classification and kernel trick for non-linear boundaries.
svm_visualization.name: Support Vector Machine Visualization
svm_visualization.qfep_connection: SVM finds the maximum-margin boundary — the F-minimal separation between classes. Support vectors are the critical data points where the decision boundary is defined. The kernel trick lifts data to higher dimensions for linear separability: same F-minimization strategy as homogeneous coordinates.

switchboard_attention.description: Switchboard model of attention — input-output connections routed dynamically, like a telephone operator connecting callers. Attention as learned routing rather than spotlight focusing.
switchboard_attention.name: Switchboard Attention
switchboard_attention.qfep_connection: Attention as a switchboard — connections routed dynamically, many lines patched at once. The transformer's ancestor-metaphor: not a beam but a wiring diagram that reconfigures per moment, relevance as routing.

time_series_analysis.description: Temporal pattern recognition — sliding windows, autocorrelation, seasonal decomposition. Algorithms that learn from sequential data.
time_series_analysis.name: Time Series Analysis
time_series_analysis.qfep_connection: Sliding windows, autocorrelation, seasonal decomposition — the instruments that find pattern in time. The past interrogated for rhythm: what repeats, what trends, what is left over — and the leftover is where the surprises live.

transformers.description: Transformer architecture visualization — self-attention, multi-head attention, positional encoding. The architecture behind GPT, BERT, and the current AI revolution.
transformers.name: Transformers
transformers.qfep_connection: The transformer opened at gallery scale — self-attention, multi-head, positional encoding. Every token weighing every other at once: the architecture that traded memory's march for relevance computed in parallel, and now reads the world.

transformers_vr.description: Interactive transformer with attention beam visualization
transformers_vr.name: Transformers_VR
transformers_vr.qfep_connection: Attention drawn as beams — every token reaching to every other, weighting what matters, and the whole sequence understood at once instead of in order. The architecture underneath the machine writing these very words: not memory marched step by step, but relevance computed all at once. The room where the curriculum quietly meets the intelligence walking it.

vaes.description: VAE visualization — encoder compresses to latent space, decoder reconstructs. The bottleneck forces meaningful representations, and the variational bound enables generation of new samples.
vaes.name: Variational Autoencoders
vaes.qfep_connection: The VAE's hourglass — encoder compressing to a latent space, decoder reconstructing, the middle a learned geometry of possibility. Compression as understanding's cheapest test: what survives the squeeze is what the model believes matters.

variational_autoencoders_vaes_vr.description: Walkable latent space with reparameterization trick
variational_autoencoders_vaes_vr.name: VariationalAutoencodersVAEs_VR
variational_autoencoders_vaes_vr.qfep_connection: Latent space at body scale: a sphere you walk into, sample points you grab, encoder and decoder tunnels compressing on one side and reconstructing on the other. The reparameterization trick is staged too — even here, chance must be smuggled past the optimizer in a differentiable envelope.

adaboost.name: AdaBoost
adaboost.description: Watch a sequence of weak learners focus on what the previous ones got wrong. Each decision stump is simple — a single threshold on one axis. But AdaBoost weights misclassified points heavier, so each new stump specializes on the hard cases. Points that keep getting misclassified visually grow larger. The ensemble decision boundary gets progressively more sophisticated from trivially simple components.
adaboost.qfep_connection: Lambda-tuning — the alpha weight per stump is the lambda that tunes how much each weak learner contributes. The ensemble is a weighted sum where lambda encodes earned trust.
adaboost.gamwell_reference: Boosting algorithms, Freund and Schapire 1997, ensemble learning, bias-variance tradeoff, weak learner aggregation
interactions: watch stumps grow round by round
observe misclassified points growing larger as weight increases
see the decision boundary evolve from simple to complex
adaboost.capacity: EXPLAIN how AdaBoost builds a strong classifier from weighted weak learners by focusing each round on previously misclassified samples.

random_forest.name: Random Forest
random_forest.description: A forest of decision trees grows one by one, each trained on a random bootstrap sample with random feature selection. Individual trees overfit — their boundaries are jagged and noisy. But the majority vote of all trees produces a smooth, generalizing boundary. Tree columns light up as each tree joins the ensemble. The decision boundary visibly smooths with each addition. Democracy applied to prediction.
random_forest.qfep_connection: E(S) filtered through Form — each tree sees random entropy (bootstrap + feature randomness) but the ensemble vote is the Form that filters noise into signal. More trees = more stable Form.
random_forest.gamwell_reference: Random forests, Breiman 2001, bagging, bootstrap aggregation, Gini impurity, ensemble diversity
interactions: watch trees grow one by one
observe tree columns lighting up as they join
see the boundary smooth as more trees vote
random_forest.capacity: EXPLAIN how Random Forest uses bootstrap sampling and random feature selection to build diverse trees whose majority vote generalizes better than any single tree.

learn_input_pair_stand.name: Learn Input-Pair Stand
learn_input_pair_stand.description: Two pillars input and output with paired tokens connected by glowing threads. A glyph drifts toward the mean output. The ML learn affordance demo.

model_seam.description: The machine-learning seam - Ada reading herself. A ReLU network is piecewise-linear: on the data (white) the blue model hugs the true amber function; off the data it extrapolates a straight line, confident and wrong. The compressed record close-reading its own compression.
model_seam.name: Model Seam
model_seam.qfep_connection: A station in the bias landscape (doc/SEAM_PER_SEQUENCE.md); the digital-bias seam for machinelearning. Bias is conserved; show the seam.
